front.title: Identity Pronouns: A Client-Side Shorthand for ~handle References and the Rule That Keeps It Off the Wire

abstract.t: A client that lets a person type a short reference such as ~org in place of a concrete ~handle has to replace the reference before anything is sent. This document states the one rule a receiver can check, that a typed handle field in a payload crossing a trust boundary never carries such a reference, and describes the client- side resolution that makes the rule hold. A reference of this kind is called a pronoun. The document defines one pronoun, ~org. It resolves to the organisation bound to the caller's current session. Resolution is local to the client and uses no network exchange. The document is Informational. It describes a convention that no second party implements, and it makes no claim that the convention needs standardising.
